chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara, who said:

We said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'How is the asking to Allah, Blessed and Exalted?' He said, 'You extend your palms.' We said, 'How is the seeking of Refuge?' He said, 'You display with your palms; and the devotion is the gesturing with the finger; and the beseeching is moving the finger; and the invoking is that you extend your hands together.'
ai.seo_question: What are the correct physical gestures for supplication (dua) and seeking refuge according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the somatic dimensions of du'a, distinguishing between the physical postures of humility (tabattul) and intense supplication (ibtilal) as articulated by Imam al-Sadiq. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the unity of body and spirit in worship, where specific gestures like finger movement or full hand extension reflect varying degrees of spiritual presence and need.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim and Zurara who both said,

‘We said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘How is the asking to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High (supposed to be)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Extending your palms’. We said, ‘How is the seeking of the Refuge (supposed to be)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Displaying with your palms; and the devotion is the gesturing with the finger; and the beseeching is moving the finger; and the invoking is that you extend your hands together’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Zurara who have said the following: “Zurara has said, ‘Once we asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) how to plead before Allah for help?’

The Imam said, ‘Stretch your palms.’ We then asked, ‘How is seeking refuge?’ The Imam said, ‘Turn your palm to Ka’aba, and al-Tabattul is making gestures with your finger. Al-Tadarru ’ is the moving of fingers and al-‘Ibtihal is the stretching out of both hands.’”
